title: Shout
description:
Write two functions that show the two reasons to use a reference:

- `void toUpperInPlace(std::string& text)` changes the caller's string, turning every letter into upper case.
- `std::string shout(const std::string& text)` leaves the caller's string alone and returns a new one: the upper-case version with `"!"` on the end.

`shout` should reuse `toUpperInPlace` on a copy rather than repeating its loop.

`std::toupper` from `<cctype>` converts one character. It takes and returns an `int`, so convert back to `char`.
hints: An index loop works: `text[i] = static_cast<char>(std::toupper(static_cast<unsigned char>(text[i])));` for every `i` from 0 to `text.length() - 1`.

The shorter range-based loop `for (char c : text)` (lesson 5.01) hands you each character in turn, but as a copy. To change the characters, the loop variable must itself be a reference: `for (char& c : text)`.
